hooks.statusMessage: Running lint, type-check and tests before commit...

hooks.prompt:
A `git push` is about to run: $ARGUMENTS

First, check whether there is anything new to push: current branch (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`), its upstream if any, and `git log @{u}.. --oneline` (or compare against the target the push command names, e.g. `origin/<branch>`, if there is no upstream yet). If there are zero new commits (a branch delete, an already-pushed branch, a tag push, etc.), allow immediately without further review.

Otherwise, review the commits that are about to be pushed but are not yet on the remote: read the diff (`git diff @{u}...HEAD` or equivalent) and check it against this repo's CLAUDE.md files (root `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`) for real correctness bugs and violations of the project's core engineering rules (server-authoritative writes, compute-on-read stats, definition/instance split, registry-driven extensibility, the point-buy/item-budget rules, etc.). Do not nitpick style, formatting, or raise speculative/low-confidence concerns — only flag issues you are confident are real problems.

Respond with ONLY one JSON object and nothing else (no other text):

If you found a real, fixable problem:
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": "<concise, specific description of what's wrong and where, enough to fix from>"}}

If there is nothing to push, or the review found no real blocking issues:
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "allow", "permissionDecisionReason": "Reviewed, no blocking issues."}}
